ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories must undergo rigorous screening against the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) designated list, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and EU sanctions lists. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs, including family members and close associates) from foreign jurisdictions. Continuous transaction monitoring and adverse media checks are mandatory. For healthcare-related IT sectors, additional verification of medical licensing and business permits is required to ensure no improper affiliations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Service (I-NET, www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in Korean (Hangul); English names are permitted as a secondary trade name but not for statutory registration. The name must follow a four-fold structure: distinctive element, business objective, legal form suffix (e.g., Chusik Hoesa), and optional proper noun. Phonetic transliteration of foreign names is required, and the chosen Hangul rendering must not conflict with existing registered trademarks or trade names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file a written objection with the Registrar detailing the basis for registrability within 14 days of rejection. The appeal must cite the relevant provisions of the Commercial Act and demonstrate that the proposed name does not infringe existing trade names. If the Registrar affirms rejection, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit with the Seoul Administrative Court. For names rejected due to social order or public interest concerns, a separate submission to the Ministry of Justice may be made.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox services are generally not accepted for VAT registration and corporate banking in Korea. The National Tax Service requires a physical location where business records are kept and accessible. For a healthcare EMR SaaS company, a registered office with actual presence is mandatory to obtain a business license (saupja-deungrok) and to meet data localization requirements under the Network Act. A virtual address may be accepted for initial registration but will significantly hamper bank account opening and license approval. We recommend leasing a physical office suite in Seoul or Busan.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspections by municipal tax authorities (National Tax Service) or the registry court are possible. Risk level: Medium (approximately 30%) during the first year for IT companies. Checklist includes: presence of employees, company signage, authenticity of lease contract, physical servers or equipment, and accessibility to accounting records. Failure to pass inspection can result in registration revocation or tax penalties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Act No. 1000, promulgated August 27, 1962, as subsequently amended, including Articles 288, 289, 290, 291, 292, 295, 296, 300, 301, 317, 318, 329, 332, 335, 363, 383, 389, 390, 391, 393, 397, 401-2, 414, 434, 461, and 543; the Regulation on the Registration of Corporate Names; the Framework Act on Registration of Real Estate and Corporate Registration; and the Act on the Registration of Real Estate and Enterprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Office of the competent Korean District Court; for a Seoul-registered entity, the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office, also accessible through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Chusik Hoesa), supported by Notarized Articles of Incorporation and the Certificate of Deposit of Subscription Price, filed under Article 317 of the Commercial Act and the Korean Court Registration Rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: There is no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa under the current Korean Commercial Act. The Articles of Incorporation must state the total number of shares and a par value of at least 100 Korean Won per share. The full subscription price for all issued shares must be paid into a blocked deposit or escrow account at a Korean licensed bank before the incorporation registration is filed. The bank must issue a Certificate of Deposit of Subscription Price, and the funds may not be withdrawn until the incorporation registration has been completed and the company acquires legal personality.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF THE CHUSIK HOESA (STOCK CORPORATION) DESCRIBED IN THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION DATED [DATE]. RESOLUTION NO. 2026-001. ADOPTED ON [DATE], AT THE PRINCIPAL OFFICE IN SEOUL, REPUBLIC OF KOREA. PRESENT: [DIRECTOR NAMES] AS DIRECTORS, CONSTITUTING A QUORUM UNDER ARTICLE 391 OF THE KOREAN COMMERCIAL ACT AND ARTICLE [NUMBER] OF THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION. THE MEETING WAS DULY CONVENED WITH NOTICE GIVEN TO ALL DIRECTORS. WHEREAS THE COMPANY WAS ORGANIZED AS A KOREAN CHUSIK HOESA UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA; WHEREAS ALL SHARES SUBSCRIBED AT INCORPORATION HAVE BEEN SUBSCRIBED IN FULL AND THE FULL SUBSCRIPTION PRICE HAS BEEN PAID INTO A LOCKED DEPOSIT ACCOUNT AT [BANK NAME] AS EVIDENCED BY THE BANK CERTIFICATE OF DEPOSIT DATED [DATE] ISSUED IN ACCORDANCE WITH ARTICLE 295 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT; AND WHEREAS THE BOARD MUST RATIFY THE CAPITALIZATION, AUTHORIZE BANKING ARRANGEMENTS, ADOPT THE REGISTERED OFFICE, AND APPOINT THE STATUTORY OFFICERS BEFORE FILING OF THE INCORPORATION REGISTRATION WITH THE COMPETENT DISTRICT COURT REGISTRY. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. THE BOARD RATIFIES THE SUBSCRIPTION SCHEDULE UNDER WHICH THE TOTAL ISSUED SHARES OF [NUMBER] COMMON SHARES, PAR VALUE KRW [AMOUNT] PER SHARE, WERE FULLY SUBSCRIBED AND FULLY PAID. THE BOARD CONFIRMS THAT THE TOTAL PAID-IN CAPITAL IS KRW [AMOUNT] AND THAT THE SUBSCRIPTION MONEY IS HELD IN THE LOCKED DEPOSIT ACCOUNT PENDING REGISTRATION. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. THE BOARD AUTHORIZES THE REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR AND [OFFICER NAME], ACTING JOINTLY OR EITHER ACTING ALONE AS THE BOARD MAY DESIGNATE, TO OPEN, OPERATE, AND ENDORSE ACCOUNTS WITH DEPOSIT BANKS, SECURITIES FIRMS, AND LICENSED FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS, TO SIGN CHECKS, MONEY TRANSFER INSTRUCTIONS, DISCOUNT AGREEMENTS, AND AUTHORIZATION LETTERS, AND TO FILE FOREIGN EXCHANGE REPORTS. THE BANK MAY RELY ON THE SPECIMEN SIGNATURES LODGED WITH IT WITHOUT FURTHER INQUIRY. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. THE BOARD ADOPTS AS THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY THE ADDRESS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE [NUMBER] OF THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION, BEING [STREET ADDRESS], SEOUL, REPUBLIC OF KOREA, AND DIRECTS THE REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR TO FILE THE INCORPORATION REGISTRATION WITH THE REGISTRY OFFICE OF THE COMPETENT DISTRICT COURT AND TO INSPECT THE REGISTERED OFFICE AND POST ANY REQUIRED NOTICE. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. THE BOARD APPOINTS [NAME] AS REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR AND CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER, [NAME] AS DIRECTOR, AND [NAME] AS AUDITOR, IF AN AUDITOR IS REQUIRED, EACH FOR A TWO-YEAR TERM COMMENCING FROM THE DATE OF REGISTRATION. THE REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR IS AUTHORIZED TO PREPARE AND SIGN THE REGISTRATION APPLICATION, TO PROCURE THE CORPORATE SEAL, TO SELECT ACCOUNTING AND LEGAL ADVISERS, AND TO EXECUTE ALL DOCUMENTS NECESSARY TO CARRY OUT THESE RESOLUTIONS. 5. THE BOARD AUTHORIZES THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER AND THE CORPORATE SECRETARY, IF APPOINTED, TO MAKE ALL REGISTRATIONS WITH THE NATIONAL TAX SERVICE, LOCAL TAX OFFICE, LABOR AGENCIES, AND RECURRENT THIRD PARTIES, AND TO DO EVERY ACT NEEDED TO GIVE FULL EFFECT TO THE FOREGOING. ADOPTED UNANIMOUSLY BY THE DIRECTORS PRESENT. THIS RESOLUTION SHALL REMAIN IN FORCE UNTIL AMENDED BY THE BOARD OR THE GENERAL MEETING OF SHAREHOLDERS. DATED [DATE] 2026. CHAIR OF THE MEETING [NAME]. SECRETARY [NAME].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office for corporate name search; Korean Notary Public under the Notary Act for authentication of the Articles of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name search on the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office to confirm that the proposed Korean trade name is not identical to an existing commercial name and is not prohibited by public order. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean with all mandatory provisions, including corporate purpose, trade name, total number of shares, par value, paid-in capital, registered office in Korea, method of notice and publication, and the number of directors. After each incorporator signs and seals the Articles, the Articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public in accordance with the Notary Act and Article 292 of the Commercial Act. The notary verifies the identity of each incorporator, the legality of the provisions, and the regularity of the incorporation procedure. Deliver the notarized Articles and certified copies to counsel for use in the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Corporate name search output or trade name existence certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation in Korean language
Passport or Alien Registration Card of each individual incorporator
Legal entity incorporation certificate and board resolution if a corporate shareholder participates
Power of attorney to local counsel for filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed trade name is rejected because of similarity to an existing name, submit an amended application with alternative names and obtain a fresh name search result. If the notary raises a substantive objection to an article, amend the relevant provision, have all incorporators re-execute the document, and cause the Articles to be re-notarized before proceeding.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Deposit Account and Full Payment of Subscription Price
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean licensed bank or financial institution acting as a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Financial Supervisory Service licensed institutions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked business deposit account in the name of the company in formation at a Korean bank or licensed financial institution. Each subscriber executes a subscription statement and pays the full subscription amount into the designated account. Korean-resident and non-resident subscribers must state their name, shareholding, number of shares subscribed, and amount paid. If any subscriber is a foreign person or foreign legal entity, a foreign exchange remittance report must be filed with the appointed bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and the bank may require a passport, Alien Registration Card, or corporate resolution of the foreign subscriber. After collection of the full amount, the bank issues a Certificate of Deposit of Subscription Price showing that the capital has been deposited. The deposited capital is blocked and may not be withdrawn until the incorporation registration has been completed.
required_dossiers: Subscription statements executed by each subscriber
Bank transfer records and inward remittance receipts
Foreign exchange transaction report or currency declaration, if applicable
Certificate of Deposit of Subscription Price issued by the Korean bank
Personal identification documents of each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the deposit or requests enhanced due diligence, provide source-of-funds evidence and ultimate beneficial owner declarations. If the deposit certificate contains discrepancies, ask the bank to reissue a corrected certificate. If a foreign remittance is rejected due to remitter mismatch, obtain amended beneficiary instructions and have the sender re-transfer the same amount into the blocked account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Stock Corporation Incorporation Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Office of the competent Korean District Court, with electronic filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa with the Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office. The filing must be made within two weeks after the full subscription price has been paid and the bank certificate obtained. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the Certificate of Deposit of Subscription Price, subscription and payment statements, minutes of the first board of directors meeting or equivalent corporate authorization, officer appointment and acceptance documents, specimen seals of the Representative Director and the company seal, and a power of attorney if filed through counsel. Pay the registration license tax, local education tax, and court fee calculated by the registry. The registration officer examines the legality of the incorporation, full payment of subscription money, and the validity of officer appointments. Upon approval, the company is entered into the Commercial Registration Register and acquires legal personality.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation of a stock corporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of Deposit of Subscription Price
Minutes of the first board of directors resolution
Consent and acceptance letters of directors, Representative Director, and auditor, if any
Specimen of corporate seal and director seals
Power of attorney, if filed through counsel
Receipt or confirmation of payment of registration tax, local education tax, and court fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a request for correction or supplementation, respond within two weeks through the Internet Registration Office. If the application is rejected because of a substantive omission, cure the defect by filing corrected documents and refiling after obtaining a new deposit certificate if necessary. An adverse registration decision may be protested or appealed under the applicable court registration procedure, but refiling is normally faster and less costly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Business Taxation, Social Insurance, and Health-Data Compliance for Medical EMR SaaS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district tax office; local municipal tax office; Korea National Pension Service; National Health Insurance Service; Korea Employment and Welfare Information Service; Korea Workers Compensation and Welfare Service; Personal Information Protection Commission; and, only if medical-device diagnostic software is later added, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty days after the issuance of the Company Registration Certificate, file an application for a Business Registration Certificate with the district tax office of the National Tax Service to obtain the corporate number for corporate tax, value-added tax, withholding, and local income tax. Register as an employer with the four major social insurance authorities and submit the business owner registration, director identification, employee data, and payroll information. For the medical EMR SaaS activity, implement a personal information protection compliance program under the Personal Information Protection Act, appoint a privacy officer, and execute data processing agreements with each medical clinic before accessing electronic medical records. Consider a privacy impact assessment with the Personal Information Protection Commission because medical information is sensitive personal data under Korean law. Confirm in writing that the EMR workflow software does not contain diagnostic or therapeutic functions that would require registration as medical device software under the Medical Devices Act; if such functions are introduced later, obtain a separate product classification from the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety. Operate only after ordinary workplace safety and building fire safety requirements have been satisfied.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate or corporate registration abstract
Business registration application form of the National Tax Service
Lease agreement for the registered office
Certificate of Deposit of Subscription Price or opening bank account documents
Director and employee identification documents
Four major social insurance employer registration forms
Privacy impact assessment or PIPA compliance documentation
Data processing agreement templates for the medical clinic EMR service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office or social insurance system returns the application for correction, use the HomeTax and Ministry of Employment and Labor electronic correction channels to submit the missing information. If the Personal Information Protection Commission requests additional safeguards for medical information, execute the remedial measures and resubmit the compliance documentation before processing any live patient data. If the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety states that the software qualifies as medical device software, suspend direct operation of the affected module and file the applicable medical device notification or approval through the relevant administrative pathway.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 6201 is computer programming and digital software publishing with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial or manufacturing operating permit is required. The separate statutory Korean Business Registration Certificate is a tax registration obligation, not an industrial operating license, and is obtained in Step 4 of the formation SOP.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Korea
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Not Applicable for an office-based digital software company; there is no physical project, facility construction, or environmental discharge triggering an EIA threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - there are no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams from the ISIC 6201 activity. If the company later leases a physical warehouse or manufactures hardware, it must then comply with the Framework Act on Environmental Policy and check the applicable scale-based EIA thresholds before any physical operation begins.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial or civil-defense permit. Ordinary office workplace safety under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and building fire safety under the Act on Fire Prevention and Safety of Buildings apply to the registered office, but no specialized Civil Defense fire permit is triggered by a software-as-a-service EMR business operating from a standard commercial office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS); electronic online portal: NTS HomeTax (hometax.go.kr) for business registration, tax filings, and electronic tax invoice clearance; Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr) for export declarations and trade filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing or operating as a Chusik Hoesa, the procedure is as follows: (1) Determine the Korean tax residence: a foreign-incorporated entity becomes a Korean domestic corporation if its head office, place of effective management, or registered office is in Korea; a pure foreign corporation without a domestic place of business must nevertheless obtain a Business Registration Number (BRN, the 10-digit TIN used for both corporate income tax and VAT) before making taxable supplies in Korea or claiming input-tax refunds. (2) File a business registration application with the competent NTS district tax office, or remotely through NTS HomeTax using an accredited digital certificate. (3) Attach the statutory dossier: foreign certificate of incorporation, articles of association (apostilled or consular-legalized as applicable), board resolution or power of attorney appointing a Korean tax representative, passport or ID copies of the representative, and evidence of the Korean place of business or service activity (for example, lease agreement, client contract, or bank account details). (4) If the foreign entity has no Korean business office, the NTS may require the appointment of a tax representative resident in Korea to receive notices and perform compliance duties. (5) After verification, the NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) constituting the entity's TIN and VAT registration. (6) The BRN holder must enrol for electronic tax invoice issuance through NTS HomeTax and keep its NTS e-authentication credentials current; a foreign person may delegate HomeTax functions to the Korean tax representative. The application should be lodged before business commencement or within 20 days of commencement to avoid penalty.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box pass-through election; a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily taxed as a separate domestic corporation on worldwide income. No hybrid-mismatch check-the-box election exists under the Corporate Tax Act. Separately, a resident parent corporation may elect consolidated corporate income tax filing for 100-percent-owned domestic subsidiaries with NTS approval, but that election does not change the entity-level classification of the Chusik Hoesa.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic turnover threshold (0 KRW). Registration is mandatory upon business commencement; the application is due within 20 days of the business-commencement date. The simplified taxpayer threshold applicable to individual sole proprietors is unavailable to a Chusik Hoesa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory national electronic invoicing and fiscal clearance regime. All B2B VAT tax invoices must be issued electronically through NTS HomeTax or an approved ERP/API-linked e-invoice system and transmitted to the NTS in real time. The NTS validates each e-tax invoice and assigns a unique NTS approval number; there is no physical fiscal-stamping hardware. The tax invoice must be issued no later than the day after the supply date, subject to the limited statutory lump-sum issue schedule. Anti-fraud controls derive from real-time NTS clearance and matching of e-invoices, entity-level digital certificates, and administrative penalties for missing, late, or false e-invoice transmissions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act, a 0% rate applies to exported goods and to services supplied for use or performance outside Korea, including qualifying offshore digital services. The EMR clinical workflow SaaS supplied by the Korean Chusik Hoesa to foreign medical clinic customers qualifies as a zero-rated export only when the recipient is a non-resident foreign entity, the service is consumed outside Korea, the supply agreement clearly provides for an offshore SaaS export, and the consideration is received in foreign currency through Korean foreign exchange banking channels. The supplier must prove the foreign place of supply and foreign-currency repatriation; a foreign address on the invoice alone is insufficient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration or Export Clearance Certificate prepared through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system, containing the export declaration number and HS/statistical code; for pure online SaaS exports, a UNI-PASS electronic export filing should be made where required, otherwise the service-performance evidence bundle below substitutes for customs clearance

Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other transport or electronic delivery evidence proving physical exportation (for physical media or software carriers); for online-only SaaS, delivery and usage records serve as the export performance evidence
Commercial invoice describing the EMR SaaS, supply terms, contract value, and 0% VAT statement
International service contract or purchase order executed with the foreign medical clinic customer

Foreign Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or foreign exchange earning certificate issued by the Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of payment in foreign currency from the overseas customer
Service performance records demonstrating offshore use (for example, go-live certificate, subscription activation log, server access or usage data, or customer acceptance email)
Foreign exchange bank record of repatriation within the 180-day statutory deadline, or an approved extension where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS audit teams cross-check export declarations, FIRCs, service contracts, e-invoice output, and payment receipts. If zero-rating is denied, the Chusik Hoesa becomes liable for the 10% VAT on the full supply value, plus the VAT Act additional tax attributable to unregistered supplies, unfaithful returns, or false e-tax invoices, and late-payment interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Intentional or fraudulent claims attract aggravated penalty tax and may be referred for prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment up to ten years or a fine not exceeding three times the tax evaded. The NTS may reopen returns within five years of the statutory due date, or ten years where the error is fraudulent or tax-avoidance-related, and any refunded VAT is clawed back with statutory interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Foreign Exchange Administration of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and its Enforcement Decree.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime with full current-account convertibility and substantial but regulated capital-account convertibility. The national currency, the Korean won (KRW), cannot be used offshore except through licensed FX banks; all resident-to-non-resident and non-resident-to-resident exchanges must be executed by a licensed foreign exchange bank and reported into the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS). For a Korean Chusik Hoesa, all software export receipts, including EMR subscription revenues collected via Stripe Billing, must be repatriated as foreign-currency receipts. Profit remittance in the form of dividends is freely transferable provided that the foreign shareholder submits the audited financial statements, a board resolution approving dividends, the corporate registration extract, and the National Tax Service withholding tax clearance. Inbound equity capital requires a proper filing under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) and opens a foreign investment capital deposit account. No fixed surrender ratio is imposed today, but export proceeds must be retained in a domestic FX account or converted by a bank. The regime is generally favourable for a treasury function, but every operation must be documented against the real commercial transaction and must be cleared by the bank's sanctions and AML engine.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under FETA and the Foreign Exchange Business Regulations, export proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic Korean foreign-currency account within one month of the receipt date. There is no mandatory conversion ratio currently in force; the exporting company is free to hold the foreign currency in its bank account, convert to KRW at market rates, or use it for permitted FX payments. All repatriations must be documented in FEIS with the export invoice and contract, along with shipping/document tracking evidence for physical goods (for software, the SaaS/service contract and electronic delivery records).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, only licensed foreign exchange banks may operate foreign-currency deposit, forward, and cross-border clearing services for resident entities. Offshore digital EMI providers such as Wise, Airwallex, and Payoneer do not hold a Korean FX banking licence and cannot accept deposits or issue bank guarantees for a Korean company. They may be used only as ancillary payment aggregation for international e-commerce/SaaS receivables, but the company must maintain its primary operating and escrow accounts with a licensed Tier-1 domestic bank. Any attempt to use an unlicensed EMI for capital outflow, intercompany loans, or dividend repatriation will be rejected by the customs/forex reporting system and is structurally non-compliant.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a low-risk technology entity, Korean Tier-1 banks will generally accept a remote/consularised onboarding route: the statutory director may execute the relationship through a notarized or apostilled board resolution and complete a video KYC interview with the bank's compliance team; the director does not have to be present in-branch for the standard operations account. However, for the Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account, or if a non-resident shareholder holds more than 30% equity, the bank's enhanced due diligence policy may require the statutory director or the appointed power-of-attorney holder to attend one face-to-face interview at a designated branch (e.g., Yeouido or Gangnam) to verify the original passport and seal. Remote consular proxy opening is only recognised if the corporate record book, passport, and financial evidence are notarised in the shareholder's jurisdiction and then apostilled or consularised, and if the bank's legal counsel accepts the proxy's identity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin corporate substance and non-resident UBO: the Chusik Hoesa is majority-owned by a foreign investor, and the board may have no Korean resident director, making it difficult for the bank to verify operational control and source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation and bylaws with an English/Korean translation; a current shareholder and beneficiary ownership register; board minutes appointing the Korean resident representative director and the authorised bank signatory; audited financial statements of the investor or an unqualified statement of net worth combining the source of funds; a recent six-month bank statement of the investor's home-country account; and a copy of the investor's passport or company extract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguity in the source of establishment capital: foreign wiring from a juridical person with potential tax haven or offshore character, or from a relative of the Korean representative, conflicts with the strict anti-money-laundering requirement to establish economic purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A capital formation schedule traceable to invoice/servicing agreements and transactional history; a specific declaration of the economic rationale for using the Chusik Hoesa; the entity's open source contracts and payroll evidence; copies of the underlying bank checks or wire memos; audited tax filings such as the National Tax Service Tax Invoice; and, if applicable, the overseas investor's annual report or letter of comfort.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border software subscription receipts from Stripe Billing: the bank sees a high volume of small-value, multi-merchant payments in multiple currencies with limited documentary support, raising suspicion that those funds are mislabelled or converted disguised funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An export service declaration that reconciles all reported Stripe settlement aggregates with the customer subscription contract list (with clinic names, licences, and deployed modules); the latest Stripe settlement report in English; the National Tax Service export sales statement and VAT invoices; and a written description of the EMR platform to demonstrate that it is a legitimate software product, not a money-exchange front.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Privacy-sensitive health-sector exposure: EMR software stores protected health information, and the bank may fear that the funds are derived from unlawful clinical data trading or that the company violates the Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) and Biohealth law.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of statutory licences and registration: PIPA compliance, ISMS-P certification or independent privacy impact assessment, medical device software permits where applicable, GDPR/HIPAA certifications if relevant, the employed data protection officer's appointment letter, and samples of compliant processing agreements with Korean medical clinics. The dossier should be certified by a local statutory auditor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection from a non-resident shareholder must be filed in advance with a licensed foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The investor obtains a foreign investment notification number; then funds are remitted via SWIFT MT103 with the reference of the capital contribution and the Korean FX purpose code for direct investment (equity). The remittance is received into the Foreign Investment Capital Escrow Account maintained with the Tier-1 bank. Upon receipt, the bank issues a Foreign Capital Deposit Certificate, and after the share issuance is completed, the company files the capital subscription report to obtain a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate, which serves as the statutory capital verification evidence. The funds may then be converted to KRW and transferred to the operating account at the market exchange rate, subject to the bank's FX desk quotation. No separate remittance approval is required for qualifying FDI, but the bank will need the articles of association, investment board resolution, and confirmation that the entity is not in a restricted sector.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All foreign payments—for cloud hosting, international software licences, vendors, and dividends—must be executed by a licensed foreign-exchange bank. For trade settlements above the bank's reporting threshold, the beneficiary and purpose code must be specified; a standard SWIFT MT103 is used for general service payments. Imports of hardware or medical-adjacent infrastructure are handled through documentary collections or commercial letters of credit, while software costs are cleared as service payments. All outbound transfers must be supported by underlying commercial documentation such as contract, invoice, tax clearance, and must be submitted to the Foreign Exchange Information System through the bank's reporting module. Domestic payroll and operational disbursements in KRW are settled through the BOK-Wire+ / large-value payment system and the ACH/CTS for batch payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD forward contracts with licensed foreign exchange banks for firm export and import exposures, subject to the real-demand principle and the submission of underlying trade documents.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) concluded with a licensed bank, allowed only for bona-fide hedging of a non-KRW underlying exposure (corporate foreign-exchange risk) and not for speculative positions.

Cross-currency swaps (KRW-USD) for maturity-matched debt or equity-related working capital exposure, provided the bank has approved the underlying transaction and the swap is documented under the standard ISDA/KSAPA terms.
Currency options only when embedded in a commercial loan or trade-finance structure and fully hedged for underlying trade invoices, with the bank's compliance desk review.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' General Meeting and Approval of Annual Financial Statements; preparation and retention of signed minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Supreme Court Registration Office) only if the AGM resolution changes the board or registered officers; otherwise no external filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each business year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, on or before 31 March each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or approve financial statements exposes directors to civil liability for losses, prohibits lawful dividend distribution, and repeated nonconvening enables shareholders to petition the court for appointment of an inspector or judicial dissolution under the Korean Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Sealed Financial Statements for the business year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; 31 March for a calendar-year company; no annual exemption for zero-capital companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An omitted or materially understating corporate tax return triggers an additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes of 20 percent of unpaid tax, or 40 percent in a fraudulent non-filing case, plus daily delinquency interest for every day past the statutory due date; persistent non-filing may lead to seizure of the corporate bank account, revocation of the business registration, and refusal of a tax clearance certificate for medical-clinic or government SaaS procurement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and submission of audited financial statements to the regulator if the statutory audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and the certified external auditor's firm
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the filing deadline of the corporate income tax return; in practice by 31 March for a December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or to file the audit report constitutes a violation of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, subject to a corrective order, penalty surcharge of up to KRW 20,000,000 (approximately USD 15,000), administrative designation as a noncompliant company, and criminal fine or imprisonment for the representative; the company may also be disqualified from receiving public hospital or clinic EMR SaaS contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual or event-triggered foreign investment status report and shareholders' register update for non-resident ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) and the relevant foreign exchange bank of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any foreign share issue or transfer must be reported within 30 days from closing; if no foreign investment movement occurs, no separate annual UBO form is due to a central Korean beneficial-ownership registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A foreign-invested company that fails to report changes to capital or foreign shareholders may be subject to administrative fines, loss of tax treaty benefits, restrictions on cash dividend repatriation, and the foreign shareholder may lose foreign-investment protection until a late report is accepted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual privacy, medical-data protection and medical-device software compliance attestation (PIPA and MFDS as applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) and/or Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), depending on whether the EMR SaaS platform is registered as Software as a Medical Device
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March for the preceding calendar year; any personal information breach must be reported to the PIPC within the statutory data-breach notification window, which is 72 hours for serious cases and otherwise as prescribed for the specific breach category
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Sustained noncompliance under the Personal Information Protection Act permits tiered administrative fines based on the processor's annual worldwide revenue and criminal penalties for intentional misuse of personal health information; failure to maintain the MFDS medical-device-software license, if applicable, may halt the product and result in registration cancellation and monetary penalty.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory for a Korean Chusik Hoesa when: (i) the company is listed on a Korea Exchange market or has submitted a registration statement to offer securities to the public; or (ii) total assets on the balance sheet at the end of the immediately preceding business year equal or exceed KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000); or (iii) the Financial Services Commission designates the company as an externally-audited entity because of public interest or enforcement history. Turnover and headcount are not by themselves statutory triggers for an unlisted private stock corporation in the Republic of Korea; balance sheet scale is the controlling threshold, with separate monitoring for cross-border transfer and healthcare-data privacy risk.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for listed companies and entities electing IFRS; Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) for private unlisted Chusik Hoesa unless the company voluntarily applies K-IFRS. The financial statements must be prepared under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, the Korean Commercial Act, and the detailed accounting principles issued by the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants. For medical EMR and SaaS revenue recognition, the taxpayer must follow the relevant revenue standard under K-IFRS 1115 or the corresponding K-GAAP standard and must present prior-year comparatives in the audited annual package.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korea does not operate a one-size-fits-all annual UBO declaration for a private unlisted stock corporation. The Chusik Hoesa must keep its shareholders' register and all registered pledges current at its registered office. Any share issuance, treasury-share sale, merger, change in controlling shareholder, or cross-border transfer of equity must be recorded in the shareholders' register and, when the foreign-investment status changes, reported to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy or the designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days after the event. For health-tech contracts under the National Health Insurance system, each EMR SaaS contract will require the company to certify its complete ownership genealogy, and the external auditor will verify the shareholder register, minutes, and subscription agreements as part of the Stage 5 register audit.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges/Mortgages over the Company's Assets
Register of Registered Pledges or Security Interests on Shares
Minute Book (Shareholders' and Board of Directors' Minutes)
Settlement Books and Trial Balance Working Papers used for statutory audit

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - USD 900 per annum for a Seoul commercial registered office and professional corporate secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 20,000 per annum for a medical EMR SaaS Chusik Hoesa, with the upper range reflecting PIPA and medical-data audit scope and group consolidation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax top bracket (progressive 9% up to KRW 200 million, 19% up to KRW 20 billion, 21% up to KRW 300 billion, 24% above KRW 300 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surtax giving a 26.4% aggregate top effective rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No patent box. R&D tax credits under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act for qualifying software/health-tech R&D; foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones may qualify for a five-year corporate income tax exemption and a further two-year 50% reduction under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; foreign tax credit and indirect tax credit are available to avoid double taxation.
